title: A Precision-Steerable Electromigration Solver with Physics-Informed Adaptive Graph Partitioning
problem: Solving Korhonen's equation for multi-segment interconnect line models becomes increasingly challenging as technology scales; traditional FEM-based methods are computationally expensive.
motivation: Electromigration reliability is increasingly critical as circuit density rises; faster and more scalable EM analysis is essential for modern VLSI design.
method: Physics-Informed Message Passing Neural network (PIMNEM) architecture for solving coupled multi-domain Korhonen equations; AdaptEM incorporates hierarchical graph partitioning with unsupervised training on subgraphs and fine-tuning with boundary constraints.
key_novelty: Physics-informed graph neural networks with hierarchical adaptive partitioning for scalable multi-scale EM analysis.
contributions: Physics-Informed Message Passing (PIMNEM) architecture for coupled Korhonen equations
AdaptEM with adaptive graph partitioning and hierarchical training strategy
Hierarchical unsupervised learning framework for generalization
limitations: 0.5% accuracy trade-off; not as fast as state-of-the-art EM tools but offers superior generalization and tuning flexibility.
primary_theme: Physics-informed neural networks for EM analysis
